task_instance: Implement a press-feedback animation on a Pressable pill button in an Expo app, following the skill's build sequence: gate it (occasional/tens-of-times-a-day, purpose=feedback), pick the cheapest tool (shared value + useAnimatedStyle on the UI thread), pick properties (transform:scale only, no layout properties), pick timing (timing curve, not spring, since no finger-drag/velocity, 120ms ease-out per the duration table), keep it off the JS thread (worklet 'onPressIn'/'onPressOut', scheduleOnRN for the haptic instead of runOnJS), add a commit haptic (Haptics.selectionAsync scheduled via scheduleOnRN), and support reduced motion (useReducedMotion -> opacity-only fallback).
evidence: Created a blank-typescript Expo SDK 57 app in the work dir (npx create-expo-app@latest . --template blank-typescript). Installed react-native-reanimated, react-native-worklets, react-native-gesture-handler, expo-haptics via `npm install` (the `npx expo install` version-resolution helper itself failed with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden' when it tried to reach the React Native Directory compatibility API for an unrelated advisory check, but the underlying npm install of the packages succeeded once run directly, so the required libraries did install and resolved SDK-compatible versions from the registry). Wrote App.tsx implementing PressablePill per the skill's decision sequence (gate/purpose stated in a comment; transform+opacity via useSharedValue/useAnimatedStyle; 120ms Easing.bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) ease-out timing, not a spring, since no finger-drag; onPressIn/onPressOut worklets; Haptics.selectionAsync fired via scheduleOnRN from react-native-worklets, not the deprecated runOnJS; useReducedMotion -> opacity-only fallback; GestureHandlerRootView wrapping the app; hitSlop/pressRetentionOffset per the press rules). Verified: (1) `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes with zero errors; (2) `npx expo export --platform ios` successfully bundles the app to Hermes bytecode (1084 modules, no build errors); (3) `npx expo export:embed --platform ios --dev false` produced a plain JS bundle (build-check/ios-bundle.js) that was grepped and contains 691 occurrences of '__worklet', 4 of 'asWorklet', and 10 of 'workletHash' -- confirming babel-preset-expo's automatic Reanimated/worklets Babel plugin actually ran on the onPressIn/onPressOut functions and compiled them into real worklets (the failure mode the skill calls out, 'Failed to create a worklet at runtime', would only happen if this plugin were missing or misconfigured, which it was not). Files: App.tsx, package.json (deps added), build-check/ios-bundle.js, dist/ (Hermes export). A `web` export was also attempted for a browser-visual check but failed for a separate reason (react-native-web/react-dom not installed in this blank template, plus the same proxy network restriction on an unrelated telemetry/compat fetch) -- not pursued further since it was not needed to verify the core deliverable and actual on-device 'feel' verification is explicitly out of scope for any sandbox per the skill itself (it requires a release build on a real slowest-supported device, which no runtime -- including a full developer machine -- can substitute for).
